stem: Meena's mother gives her a mixture containing sand, common salt and water. Meena wants to collect each part separately. Which statement is correct?

options.text: One single method is enough because every mixture can be separated completely if the method is done carefully.
She needs more than one method in a sequence: filter to get the sand, then evaporate the water to get the salt.
Filtering the mixture once will collect the sand, the salt and the water separately at the same time.
Evaporating the water first will give pure salt, leaving no need for any other step.

teacher.key_rationale: A three-component mixture (sand, salt, water) needs a sequence of methods: filtration removes insoluble sand, evaporation then recovers dissolved salt from water. Only B states this; A, C and D each claim one method suffices.
